chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Ismail al-Shaeery, from Al-Hakam ibn Uteyba, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'A man gives to another man from the zakat of his wealth to perform Hajj with it.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The wealth of zakat can be used for Hajj.' So I said to him (peace be upon him), 'He is a Muslim man giving to a Muslim man.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'If he is needy, let him give to him for his need and his poverty, and he should not say to him, 'Perform Hajj with it.' He can do with it afterwards whatever he wishes.'
ai.seo_question: Can zakat money be used to perform Hajj according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the distinction between using zakat funds specifically for Hajj versus giving them to a needy Muslim for general sustenance. The Imam emphasizes that if the recipient is poor, the giver should not impose the condition that the money be used for Hajj, thereby granting the recipient full autonomy over the zakat wealth. This reflects the Shia scholarly view that zakat is a right of the poor to be spent at their discretion, rather than a restricted grant for specific acts of worship.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Jameel Bin Darraj, from Ismail Al Shaeery, from Al Hakam Bin Uteyba who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullahasws, ‘A man gives to the man from the Zakāt of his wealth what he can perform Hajj with’. Heasws said: ‘Hajj can be performed with it (the wealth of Zakāt)’. So I said to himasws, ‘He is a Muslim man giving to a Muslim’. So heasws said: ‘If he was needy, so let him give to him for his need, and his poverty, and he should not be saying to him, ‘Perform Hajj with it’. He can do whatever he so desires to with, afterwards’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Jamil ibn Darraj from ’Isma‘il al- Ash’ariy from al-Hakam ibn ‘Utaybah who has said the following: “

I once asked abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who gives Zakat to a man to perform Hajj. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is Zakat money and he performs Hajj!’ I then said, ‘It is a Muslim man who gives Zakat to a Muslim man.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘If he is needy, Zakat must be given to him for his needs and poverty, and one must not say to him to perform Hajj. It is up to him to use as he likes.’”
